item.title: Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future This November 10, in the midst of the Bitcoin Histórico conference taking place in the Historical Center of San Salvador, a group of Bitcoiners representing a wide range of sectors within the industry met with President Bukele. The dinner was organized by The Bitcoin Office, which is part of the Office of the President, and was led by Stacy Herbert and Max Keiser. The dinner went on from about 7:30 pm to 10:30 pm local time and included about thirty Bitcoiners, many regular visitors to El Salvador. Photograph by the Bitcoin Office. Among the guests was billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego, founder of Grupo Salinas, which owns Banco Azteca. Salinas is a known Bitcoiner, who has made public appearances with Keiser and Herbert in the past, and is speculated to be planning a run at the next Mexican Presidential election. Salinas met privately with the President besides the dinner and reportedly gifted him volumes one and two of Manuscripts of the Conquistadors, works curated and edited by Jorge Nikaido, Chief of Staff of Grupo Salinas. Representing investors and founders were Parker Lewis, founder of Unchained Capital, Mike Peterson of Bitcoin Beach fame, Katie Ananina of Citizen X, and Aleks Svetski, entrepreneur and founder of Satlantis. Bitcoin miners also attended, such as Beau Turner, CEO of Abundant Mines, Nacho Pauls, CCO of OCEAN Mining, and Adam Ortolf of Denver Bitcoin mining. Jon Atack, a Bitcoin core contributor, was also at the dinner alongside engineer Giacomo Zucco of Plan B Network, and AI tech entrepreneurs Ginger Gaetz of the ANIA AI initiative and Marc Seal, Founder of Aevonix. The academic and media side of the industry was also heavily represented, with none other than Michael Goldstein, also known as Bitstein and co-founder of the Nakamoto Institute. Eric Yakes, economist and author of The 7th Property , was there, as well as Efrat Feningson, independent journalist and podcaster. Local Bitcoiner Michael Ruiz also attended the dinner; he is the founder of Build in El Salvador (BIS), an increasingly popular kind of business club and Bitcoin meetup mix. Setting the Table Photograph by the Bitcoin Office. The guests arrived at the Casa Presidencial earlier in the evening and were chatting and networking while waiting for the president. Max Keiser, always a showman, arrived at the Casa Presidencial with a gift some might speculate carried a magical artefact. Photographed above, the case was said to contain a Stetson El Presidente cowboy hat, though some have speculated it might in fact have carried the Philosopher’s Stone. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides Strategy (MSTR) shares fell 4.6% on Thursday to close at $86.13, their sixth straight daily decline, as bitcoin dipped below $62,000 and a broad selloff hit U.S. stocks. In after hours trading, shares were down to $85.50. The stock opened near $93 and slid through the afternoon, finishing near its low of about $86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 1,000 points, and the Nasdaq Composite lost about 2.1%. Bitcoin touched a low of $61,658 during the session, its weakest price since July. It was back near $62,000 late in the afternoon. Strategy stock extends its slide The drop adds to a brutal month for the largest corporate holder of bitcoin. Strategy shares are down about 37% from their $136.02 close on Oct. 19, and down about 29% from the $121.07 close on Nov. 10, which is when the latest leg lower began. Thursday was the stock’s sixth consecutive losing session. The slide has wiped out most of the year’s value. Strategy closed 2025 at $151.95, which puts the stock down about 43% in 2026. The shares fell below $100 on Tuesday and now trade about 11% below Tuesday’s $96.50 close. That day they also dipped under the company’s STRC preferred for the first time since mid-August. Thursday’s move tracked bitcoin closely. Institutions have kept buying even so, and a New York state pension fund boosted its stake by more than 10% in a recent filing. The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 as traders weighed the risk of Federal Reserve rate hikes and a sharp pullback in technology stocks. Holdings now sit well below cost Strategy added 485 bitcoin in the week ending Nov. 15, according to its Nov. 16 Form 8-K. It paid $33.4 million, or an average of $68,887 per coin, and its total reached 850,849 BTC. Those coins cost $64.20 billion, or an average of $75,452 each. With bitcoin near $62,000, the stack is worth roughly $52.8 billion, which leaves Strategy with an unrealized loss of about $11 billion. Bitcoin is trading about 18% below the company’s average purchase price. The 850,849 coins are more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap, and the company also held about $4.9 billion in U.S. dollar reserves as of Nov. 15, which gives it a cushion for preferred dividends and buybacks. Strategy has not announced a new purchase since that filing. It has reported its buys on Mondays in recent weeks, so the next update would normally come Monday. Preferred buybacks take priority Most of Strategy’s recent cash has gone to its preferred stock instead of bitcoin. In the same filing, the company said it repurchased 2,282,510 shares of its STRC preferred for $228.1 million, nearly seven times what it spent on bitcoin. It funded the purchases with $244.7 million raised from selling common stock. item.title: SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas. According to the SEC’s complaint , filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed. How the scheme worked Social media ads sent prospective victims to WhatsApp group and private chats run by the scammers. People in those chats posing as investment advisers first gave advice on trading U.S. stocks, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform. The complaint says the scheme ran in four adviser and platform pairs, each active for roughly six months. Advisor WeChat Capital and Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance operated from about August to December 2024. HB Wealth Advisors and IdeaCrypto Exchange followed from January to July 2025. Convergent Wealth Advisors and RealSimple Crypto Exchange ran from about July to December 2025. Associated Wealth Advisors and Essential Crypto Exchange closed out the scheme from January to May 2026. Each pair vanished after collecting millions, the SEC said, and a new one took its place. Victims were told to buy ether, tether or USDC on a U.S. exchange and move it to a self-custody wallet. They then sent it to an address supplied by the adviser, and a realistic app showed balances and gains that were invented. When investors tried to withdraw their supposed profits, they were told they first had to pay a fee, calculated as a percentage of those profits, in crypto to a separate address. The complaint says investors who balked were threatened and pressured. Eventually the websites went down and the chats went silent. Fake certificates and real losses To look legitimate, the defendants made fake SEC certificates and pointed skeptical investors to real filings with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. The complaint says those filings carry no regulatory approval, since registering for access to its EDGAR system is ministerial and Forms ADV are not reviewed before publication. The complaint says Convergent Wealth and Essential Crypto also filed false Forms ADV listing regulatory contacts who do not appear to be real and offices in Colorado that did not exist. The SEC said a Form D and the two Forms ADV have been removed from its website. Three unnamed investors illustrate the damage. item.title: Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 on Thursday afternoon, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, extending a slide of about 24% in one month as Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut set off a broad selloff in tech stocks. Bitcoin was trading near $81,800 on Oct. 19. It touched a low of about $61,650 on Thursday, its weakest level since July, before steadying near $62,200. The drop was about 25% from the Oct. 19 close, based on daily data. The slide came in steps. Bitcoin closed near $80,050 on Oct. 25, about $78,250 on Nov. 1 and about $74,750 on Nov. 8. The steepest leg came last week, when it fell about 12.6% to a Nov. 15 close near $65,300, and the losses have continued this week. Bitcoin had climbed back to about $64,000 early Thursday as Anthropic’s record IPO lifted stock futures, as this morning’s report showed. The rally faded once U.S. markets opened. The bitcoin price fell from roughly $63,900 at the opening bell to about $62,200 by midday. Anthropic debut sparks a tech selloff Anthropic shares opened shortly before noon at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, CNBC reported. The opening trade valued the Claude maker at more than $2 trillion. The stock quickly pulled back and was last near $97, about 17% above its offering price. The broader market went the other way. The major averages fell to session lows soon after Anthropic began trading, as investors took profits on the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2% after gaining as much as 2% earlier in the session, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 1,000 points. Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told CNBC the premarket rally had faded even before Anthropic began trading. He called it the latest round of “sell the rally” trading. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 3%, and the S&P 500 headed toward a sixth straight loss, the AP reported. The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street’s fear gauge, climbed to about 28 after touching nearly 29 shortly after Anthropic began trading. That was its highest level since March, up from about 24.6 at Wednesday’s close. The bitcoin price moved in step with the Nasdaq through the afternoon. Crypto stocks erase their morning gains Crypto stocks followed the Nasdaq lower in late-afternoon trading, about 3:55 p.m. ET. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $86.70, down about 4% on the day. Galaxy Digital (GLXY) dropped about 6.9%, the steepest decline in the group. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 0.9% to near $109.50, while Circle (CRCL) fell about 2.2%. Bitcoin miners gave back their early rally too. IREN (IREN) fell about 5.6%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 5.4% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 4.2%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 2.9%. item.title: Institutions are Piling Into Bitcoin ETFs, Pushing Holdings to a Record
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Institutions are Piling Into Bitcoin ETFs, Pushing Holdings to a Record Institutions returned to U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded products as net buyers in the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record 356,491 BTC, according to a new report from Galaxy Research. Investment managers that file Form 13F with the SEC added the equivalent o f 49,229 BTC, net of sales, between July 1 and Sept. 30. That is the most since the second quarter of 2025 and more than the 47,054 BTC they sold over the previous three quarters. The holdings were worth $29.78 billion at quarter-end prices. Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, published the analysis Thursday. The buying came as bitcoin swung between a bear-market low of $57,717 on July 1 and a high of $87,397 on Sept. 21, and Galaxy said the accumulation continued through that range. Wealth platforms lead the buying Half of the net addition came from advisors and wealth platforms, a group that includes registered investment advisors, wealth managers, wirehouses and broker-dealer platforms. The category reported 144,307 BTC, or 40.5% of all 13F-reported holdings, the highest share since the funds launched in January 2024. Those firms have now been net buyers for nine straight quarters. Their holdings are 3.3 times their March 2024 level, and Galaxy said the group accounts for 100,003 of the 179,300 BTC that all filers have added since the second quarter of 2024. Wirehouses drove the quarter. The category added a record 24,838 BTC, led by Wells Fargo at 14,636 BTC, Bank of America at 7,201 BTC and Morgan Stanley at 2,875 BTC. Wells Fargo became the largest 13F holder for the first time. It reported 30,553 BTC, worth $2.55 billion, nearly double the 15,931 BTC it held on June 30, and passed Jane Street. No wealth platform had ranked first before, and Millennium Management had held the top spot in every quarter from early 2024 through the first quarter of 2026. Hedge funds step back, IBIT dominates Hedge funds now hold 19.0% of 13F-reported holdings, down from 50.6% at the end of 2024. Basis and relative-value funds hold 34,053 BTC, far below their peak of 101,826 BTC, though they and macro funds were both buyers last quarter, adding 9,184 BTC and 10,492 BTC. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounts for two-thirds of the institutional position. Filers hold 232,453 BTC in the fund, or 65.2% of everything reported, and IBIT took 34,744 BTC of the quarter’s net 49,229 BTC. Filers’ holdings of Grayscale’s GBTC fell for the 10th straight quarter, and the lower-fee Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust passed it for the first time. The number of managers holding a spot bitcoin fund rose by 191 to 2,166, the first increase after two quarters of decline. Galaxy noted that a few large firms drove the gain. item.description: ▶ Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin’s Last Line of Defense Is $58K Katie Stockton, Founder of Fairlead Strategies, joins BMTV as Bitcoin falls below its 200-week moving average, sitting at about $63,000 per the host. She says her longer-term indicators for Bitcoin are somewhat constructive, pointing to a major low in June and July near long-term support between about $58,000 and $60,000. Bitcoin is headed back toward that support on negative short-term momentum, and she says there are no signs yet that the retracement is done. As long as it holds that range, she says, it preserves the potential for a long-term basing phase, backed by indicators like the monthly MACD and monthly stochastic oscillator. item.title: Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000 Sygnum Bank estimates that bitcoin could reach a new all-time high near $128,000. The Swiss digital asset bank laid out the scenario in its 2027 Sygnal outlook on Thursday, alongside a call that bitcoin and ether will both set new highs while the broader market stays narrow. The report also frames the current downturn as the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date. Sygnum puts the drawdown at around 54%, compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles, and says digital assets enter 2027 with lower structural volatility and stronger fundamentals. The outlook arrives as bitcoin trades near $63,000 after six straight weekly losses and a drop below its 200-week moving average. Sygnum’s case is that the market has changed since earlier cycles, not that the slide is over. Sygnum describes a more mature market. Volatility is increasingly driven by broader dollar liquidity and market structure, it said, and institutions have added new channels through ETFs, leveraged trading and crypto-backed credit. By the end of October, stablecoin supply stood near $298 billion and tokenized real-world assets exceeded $39 billion. JUST IN: Switzerland's Sygnum Bank estimates that Bitcoin could hit a new high of $128,000. Its 2027 outlook also calls this Bitcoin's "shallowest bear market yet". pic.twitter.com/KWyFALBAR8 — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 19, 2026 How bitcoin gets to $128,000 The estimate rests on a rotation out of technology stocks. Digital assets are worth about 6% of the Nasdaq’s market value, and Sygnum calculates that if 0.75% of Nasdaq value, roughly $360 billion, moved into crypto, total market capitalization could rise by more than 60%. In that scenario, bitcoin would reach a new high near $128,000. The report does not put a date on it and describes the figure as an estimate built on Sygnum’s own calculations, not a price target. It also notes that a sell-off in AI stocks could spill into crypto. Currently, Anthropic’s record $81 billion IPO is set to open about 25% to 30% above its $83 offering price, which has lifted AI and chip stocks, but worries about higher interest rates have pulled the Nasdaq back from an early 2% gain to about 0.3%. Bitcoin moves into the reserve bucket Behind the price call is a shift in how institutions treat bitcoin. Sygnum predicts it will move out of the tactical sleeve of portfolios and into the “strategic reserve bucket,” competing with gold for capital that wants protection against currency debasement. BlackRock, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America each recommend allocations of 1% to 4%. The report says 2027 should reward selection over broad market exposure. Sygnum expects adoption to concentrate in stablecoins, tokenized assets, bitcoin as an institutional macro asset and tokens with proven usage, and it believes investors will be rewarded for choosing assets with real usage and revenue. item.title: CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn House Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill said the CLARITY Act is unlikely to pass before the year ends, leaving the crypto market structure bill to a new Congress that Democrats will control. Hill spoke Thursday at the Capitol Crypto Forum in Washington. “We never give up hope in a lame duck, but it is lame, and therefore the chances are not high,” the Arkansas Republican said . He added that he plans to make market structure legislation his pitch in the next Congress, which begins in January. “I regret that it was not something we could get done effectively in this Congress,” Hill said. He said 78 Democrats voted for the CLARITY Act in the House and that he expects that support to continue in the new Congress. Hill also called it encouraging that Rep. Maxine Waters, the committee’s top Democrat, circulated a memo to House Democrats naming digital asset market structure as a topic she intends to work on if she becomes chair. Senate floor time is running out Sen. Bernie Moreno, the lead sponsor of the CLARITY Act in the Senate, told the same forum there is “no scenario” in which crypto legislation passes the chamber during the lame-duck session. Funding the government, the National Defense Authorization Act and the farm bill will take priority, according to The Hill, and the session is set to end in less than a month. The Senate blocked the CLARITY Act on Sept. 15, voting 49-50 on a procedural motion that needed 60 votes. All Democrats and four Republicans opposed it, CBS News reported. Sen. Thom Tillis entered a motion to reconsider, which keeps the option of another vote alive, but the bill dies when this Congress ends Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it. The House passed the legislation 294-134 in July 2025. President Donald Trump urged lawmakers in August to send it to his desk, but Democrats objected that its ethics provisions did not go far enough to address his potential conflicts of interest in crypto, and regulators have since moved ahead on their own, including an SEC exemption for tokenized stocks. Democrats prepare to take over The industry is now scrambling to repair its relationship with Democrats, Politico reported Thursday. The industry spent $55 million trying to defeat Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio, who won his seat back, and Democrats are set to retake both the House and Senate in January. Sen. Ruben Gallego, a crypto-friendly Arizona Democrat who spent months negotiating the Senate bill, gave Politico’s Jasper Goodman a blunt assessment of the industry’s political prospects. “They’re f***ed,” Gallego said, according to a post from journalist Eleanor Terrett. Terrett has reported that House Democrats are discussing turning Waters’ Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights into their own market structure bill.
